::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[How to show that $\omega (e)$ is a $2$-cocycle on $\mathfrak g\ $?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/4621160/how-to-show-that-omega-e-is-a-2-cocycle-on-mathfrak-g), asked by [ACB](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/778190/acb) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2023-01-18; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> > Let $G$ be a Lie group with Lie algebra $\mathfrak {g}.$ Let $\omega$ be a left-invariant non-degenerate closed $2$-form on $G.$ Then $\omega (e)$ is a $2$-cocycle on $\mathfrak {g}$ i.e. $$\omega (e) ([a,b], c) + \omega(e) ([b,c], a) + \omega (e) ([c,a], b) = 0$$ for all $a,b,c \in \mathfrak {g},$ where $[\cdot, \cdot]$ is the Lie bracket on $\mathfrak {g}.$
>
> How to prove it? Any help in this regard would be warmly appreciated.
>
> Thanks for your time.
:::

First prove this lemma: If $\omega$ is a left-invariant differential $2$-form on $G$, and $X$ and $Y$ are left-invariant vector fields on $G$, with $X_e = \xi$ and $Y_e = \eta$ in $\mathfrak{g}$, then
$$\omega(X,Y)_g = \omega(X,Y)_e = \omega_e(\xi,\eta)$$
To clarify the notation:

* $\omega$ is a differential $2$-form, while $X$ and $Y$ are vector fields, so $\omega(X,Y)$ is a function on $G$. 
* $\omega(X,Y)_g$ denotes the value of that function at a point $g \in G$.
* $\omega_e$ is an element of $\left(\bigwedge^2 T_e G\right)^* = \left(\bigwedge^2 \mathfrak{g}\right)^*$. 
* $\omega_e(\xi,\eta)$ is the value of $\omega_e$ on $\xi \wedge \eta$

In particular, notice that *$\omega(X,Y)$ is a constant function on $G$.*

The proof of this lemma requires carefully writing out the definitions of left-invariant, both for vector fields and for differential forms.

Now to prove the main statement: let $\xi$, $\eta$, and $\zeta\in\mathfrak{g}$. There are unique left-invariant vector fields $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ on $G$ such that $X_e = \xi$, etc. Observe that
$$d\omega(X,Y,Z) = X \omega(Y,Z) - Y \omega(X,Z) + Z \omega(X,Y) - \omega([X,Y],Z) + \omega([X,Z],Y) - \omega([Y,Z],X)$$
Once again, to clarify the notation: $\omega(Y,Z)$ (etc.) is a function on $G$, and $X$ is a vector field on $G$. $X \omega(Y,Z)$ means the derivative of $\omega(Y,Z)$ in the direction of $Z$. This is a function on $G$.

Since $\omega$, $Y$, and $Z$ are left-invariant, $\omega(Y,Z)$ is constant. Therefore $X\omega(Y,Z) = 0$. The same for the next two terms in the expansion of $d\omega(X,Y,Z)$.

In light of the fact that $d\omega = 0$, we have
$$\omega([X,Y],Z) + \omega([Z,X],Y) + \omega([Y,Z],X) = 0$$
as functions on $G$. Evaluating at $g=e$ gives
$$\omega_e([\xi,\eta],\zeta) + \omega_e([\zeta,\xi],\eta) + \omega_e([\eta,\zeta],\xi) = 0$$
QED
